scenes.heading: Shape and spatial patterns
scenes.sub: What changed? Say it, check it, do it
scenes.say: An arrow turns, a square moves, a dot appears. Shape pattern questions have no numbers, but they still follow rules. Let us learn to spot every change.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Spot-the-difference: compare two pictures and list every change
scenes.science: Compare frames 1 and 2, name each change, then repeat it
scenes.breaks: in spot-the-difference the changes are random. In a pattern, the same change happens every step.
scenes.say: You know spot-the-difference puzzles. Compare two pictures and list every change. Shape patterns are the same, but better: the same changes happen every step, so once you have named them you can predict the next picture.

scenes.heading: Turning by 45°
scenes.say: First the frames, then the arrows. Up, up-right, right, down-right. Each step turns forty-five degrees clockwise, like a clock hand moving an hour and a half. So the next arrow points straight down, not left.
scenes.caption: Up → up-right → right → down-right: 45° clockwise each step. Next: pointing down.

scenes.heading: Use a clock for turns
points: Clockwise = the way clock hands go
scenes.say: Picture a clock. Up is twelve, right is three, down is six, left is nine. A ninety degree turn moves three hours. Forty-five degrees is an hour and a half. Clockwise is the way the hands move.

scenes.heading: Two changes at once
scenes.say: Here two things change. Watch the shapes appear: circle, square, circle, so next is a square. Now the dots: one, two, three, so next is four. The answer is a square with four dots. Track each change on its own.
scenes.caption: Shapes alternate (circle, square, circle → square). Dots go 1, 2, 3 → 4. Answer: a square with 4 dots.

scenes.heading: Matchstick patterns
scenes.question: 1 triangle uses 3 sticks, 2 use 5, 3 use 7. How many for 10 triangles?
scenes.say: Each new triangle shares a side, so it only adds two sticks. The rule is two times the triangles, plus one. For ten triangles: twenty plus one is twenty-one. Thirty counts the shared sides twice.
scenes.caption: Each new triangle adds 2 sticks. Rule: 2 × triangles + 1. For 10: 2 × 10 + 1 = 21.

scenes.heading: Reflection or rotation?
scenes.say: Do not mix up reflections and rotations. A reflection flips across a mirror line: a vertical mirror swaps left and right. A rotation turns the whole shape, and in a grid, corners stay corners and edge squares stay edge squares.

points: Check it on the next pair
scenes.say: Quick recap. Name every change and check it on the next pair. Use a clock face for turns. When two things change, track each one. And count shapes in a system. Now try the practice questions!
